reason: The sources provide sufficient corroborated claims to produce a short story.
story: For eight centuries, foreign armies had failed to breach the walls of Rome. But in 410 AD, centuries of corruption, broken promises, and political betrayal brought the Visigoths to the gates of the Eternal City. Led by King Alaric, the besiegers cut off the Tiber River, reducing citizens to starvation and desperation. On August 24, 410, the Visigoths poured through the Salarian Gate. For three days, palaces were ransacked and treasures plundered, while churches were spared. The fall of Rome shocked the ancient world, proving that even the mightiest empire could crumble from within.
angle: For the first time in nearly 800 years, Rome fell to a foreign enemy.
